intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Visit multi-floor gadget stores, retro game shops, maid cafes, and cutting-edge tech showrooms. Experience the intersection of Japanese innovation, otaku culture, and consumer electronics that defines modern Tokyo.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, strolling through the historic Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district to witness traditional festivals, rickshaw rides, and preserved Edo-period architecture.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and creativity merge into breathtaking immersive environments. Walk through rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art that redefine the boundary between viewer and artwork, perfectly blending tech culture with artistic expression.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Izakaya Alley Night Food Crawl
experiences.description: Venture into the atmospheric narrow alleys of Omoide Yokocho and Kabukicho for an authentic izakaya experience. Savor yakitori skewers, ramen, gyoza, and sake alongside local salarymen and chefs in tiny, smoke-filled stalls that have barely changed since the post-war era.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use travel time to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or Keikyu/Narita Express train to Tsukiji area (~¥1,000–¥3,000). Check in to your Tsukiji boutique stay, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tsukiji Outer Market stalls for a casual first dinner — try fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), grilled scallops, or tuna onigiri from street vendors. Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens entrance for a scenic evening view of the garden walls and Tokyo skyline along the Sumida River.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bento box or ramen at the airport before boarding or on arrival (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market street food stalls — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a filling mix of skewers, sushi bites, and tamagoyaki

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Convenience stores (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Lawson) are excellent for cheap, high-quality snacks and meals throughout your stay. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast experience. Browse the market stalls open from 05:00 — try fresh sushi sets, grilled fish, and miso soup from the many small eateries. Visit the nearby Namiyoke Inari Shrine, a charming hidden shrine dedicated to protecting fishermen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a stunning traditional garden with a tidal pond and seasonal flowers. Then head to Ginza for window shopping and people-watching along one of Tokyo's most iconic boulevards. Visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store (a Tokyo institution for stationery and design lovers) and the free Ginza Sony Park for a taste of tech culture.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Shiodome and walk along the Shiodome Caretta illumination area. Dine at one of the affordable ramen or gyoza restaurants in the Shiodome underground mall. Return to Tsukiji for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi breakfast set or tamagoyaki sandwich (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Yoshinoya or Matsuya gyudon (beef bowl) chain near Ginza (~¥500–¥700)
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local shop in Shiodome or back in Tsukiji (~¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens is especially beautiful in April with spring flowers. Ginza's main street (Chuo-dori) is pedestrianized on Sunday afternoons — note this for future planning.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa (20 min from Tsukiji). Visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple — free to enter. Explore Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional snacks like ningyo-yaki and kaminari-okoshi. Climb the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center for a free panoramic view of the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River to Sumida Park — beautiful in April with cherry blossoms or late-season flowers. Visit the free exterior of the Tokyo Skytree (enter only if budget allows — observation deck ¥2,100–¥3,100). Explore Hoppy Street in Asakusa for a retro shitamachi (old town) atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Asakusa for dinner on Hoppy Street — enjoy yakitori skewers and hoppy beer (a budget-friendly beer-like drink) at the outdoor stalls. Browse the evening atmosphere around Senso-ji, which is beautifully lit after dark.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and green tea (~¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Tempura tendon at Asakusa Mugitoro or a local tempura shop (~¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street yakitori and drinks (~¥1,200–¥1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free and open 24 hours though the main hall has set hours. Early morning visits are less crowded. Keep an eye out for rickshaw rides as a cultural photo opportunity (free to watch).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara — Tokyo's famous Electric Town and the heart of tech and otaku culture. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera (free to browse). Visit retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and maid cafes (budget ¥500–¥800 for a maid cafe experience if interested).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara's back streets for vintage electronics, Gundam model kits, and doujinshi (self-published manga). Visit the free Gachapon Kaikan (capsule toy hall) for a uniquely Japanese experience. Take the short walk or subway to Kanda Myojin Shrine — a beautiful shrine with strong ties to tech culture and IT companies.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to nearby Ochanomizu or Jimbocho for dinner. Jimbocho is Tokyo's famous book town — browse second-hand bookshops before dinner. Dine at a budget curry restaurant (Japanese curry is a local staple) in the area.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast or McDonald's Japan (try the Teriyaki Burger) (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen or katsu curry at a local chain like CoCo Ichibanya (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Jimbocho curry restaurant or soba noodle shop (~¥700–¥1,100)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best experienced on a weekend when the main street (Chuo-dori) is pedestrianized. Bring cash as many smaller shops are cash-only. Gachapon machines cost ¥200–¥500 each — a fun low-cost souvenir option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — take the subway to Harajuku Station. Explore Takeshita Street for colorful street fashion, crepes, and youth culture. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) set in a peaceful forested area — a spiritual contrast to the vibrant street outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Yoyogi Park (free) — especially lively on Sundays with street performers, picnickers, and cosplayers. Continue to Omotesando for window shopping along Tokyo's Champs-Élysées. Browse the free Omotesando Hills architecture and the basement food hall for affordable gourmet snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing experience. Visit the free Shibuya Sky observation area exterior or the free rooftop of Shibuya Scramble Square's lower floors. Dine in Shibuya's Dogenzaka or Udagawacho areas for affordable izakaya food.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or a local stand (~¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Yoyogi Park with convenience store bento (~¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Izakaya set menu in Shibuya (~¥1,200–¥2,000 with a drink)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is especially serene in the morning. Sundays in Yoyogi Park often feature live music and cultural groups. Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic at night — great for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Shinjuku. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (open from 09:00, free) for panoramic views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Shinjuku area and Shinjuku Central Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's best parks with a mix of Japanese, French, and English garden styles. Walk through the lively Kabukicho entertainment district (safe to visit in daytime) and explore the Golden Gai alleyway — a famous cluster of tiny bars and a cultural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori and ramen stalls with a retro Showa-era atmosphere. Perfect for a budget dinner with grilled skewers and cold beer.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or bakery near Tsukiji (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic with convenience store bento or sandwiches (~¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori and beer (~¥1,500–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building North Tower observation deck is free but check for closure dates. Shinjuku Gyoen does not allow alcohol inside. Golden Gai bars are very small (5–8 seats) and atmospheric — some charge a small cover fee of ¥500.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — take the Yurikamome Line from Shimbashi (scenic monorail ride with great bay views, ~¥330). Visit the free teamLab Digital Art Museum exterior and DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size RX-78-2 Gundam statue (free). Explore the Odaiba beachfront and the Rainbow Bridge views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) lobby area or pay for entry (¥630) for an immersive tech and science experience — perfect for tech culture enthusiasts. Browse the Toyota Mega Web (free) or the Palette Town shopping complex. Enjoy the futuristic cityscape of Odaiba.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via the scenic Yurikamome Line at sunset for beautiful bay views. Dine near Shimbashi station at one of the many salaryman izakayas — affordable, authentic, and lively.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court at DiverCity or Aqua City (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya salaryman set (~¥1,000–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is excellent for tech culture interests — exhibits cover robotics, AI, and space exploration. The Yurikamome Line offers some of the best views of Tokyo Bay — sit at the front for the best experience. Check teamLab Borderless reopening status as it relocated.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno — take the subway to Ueno Station. Explore Ueno Park (free) — one of Tokyo's most beloved public parks with museums, a zoo, and Shinobazu Pond. Visit the free exterior of the Tokyo National Museum (entry ¥1,000 if budget allows — highly recommended for culture enthusiasts) and Toshogu Shrine (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Ameyoko Market — a vibrant outdoor market street near Ueno Station selling street food, clothing, cosmetics, and fresh produce. Great for budget snacks and souvenir shopping. Explore the nearby Yanaka Ginza shopping street for a nostalgic shitamachi (old downtown) atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Yanaka or Nezu neighborhood — one of Tokyo's most preserved old-town areas with affordable local restaurants. Try a local izakaya or a traditional Japanese set meal (teishoku) for an authentic cultural dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Ameyoko street food — try karaage chicken, taiyaki, or fresh seafood (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Yanaka teishoku set meal at a local restaurant (~¥800–¥1,300)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is the oldest and largest museum in Japan — budget 2–3 hours if you pay entry. Yanaka is one of the few Tokyo neighborhoods that survived WWII bombings and retains an Edo-era feel. Great for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji neighborhood — a bohemian, alternative culture hub known for vintage clothing, indie music, and a laid-back atmosphere. Browse the many second-hand clothing and vintage record shops along Koenji's covered shopping arcades (Pal and Look shopping streets).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nakano Broadway — a multi-floor shopping complex famous for anime, manga, retro games, and collectibles (a more local and less touristy alternative to Akihabara). Then walk through the Nakano Sun Mall arcade for local shopping. Head back toward central Tokyo via Shinjuku.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's indie culture neighborhood known for live music, vintage shops, and a creative arts scene. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at one of the many affordable cafes or curry restaurants in the area.

meals.breakfast: Koenji local cafe or convenience store (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nakano local ramen shop or teishoku restaurant (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa curry or cafe meal (~¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Koenji and Shimokitazawa are authentic local neighborhoods that most tourists miss — great for experiencing real Tokyo youth culture. Nakano Broadway is less crowded than Akihabara and often has better prices on vintage items.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ikebukuro — explore Sunshine City, a massive complex with a free aquarium lobby, a planetarium, and the Ancient Orient Museum. Walk through the Ikebukuro underground shopping malls. Visit the free Nishi-Ikebukuro Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sugamo — known as 'Grandma's Harajuku,' this traditional shopping street (Jizo-dori) is beloved by older locals and offers a completely different cultural perspective. Visit Koganji Temple and browse the local shops selling traditional sweets and clothing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji area for a relaxed evening. Visit the Tsukiji Outer Market evening vendors for fresh sushi or grilled items. Walk along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a scenic evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Ikebukuro food court or local ramen (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market sushi or seafood (~¥1,000–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Sugamo is a fascinating cultural contrast to the youth-oriented areas visited earlier in the trip. The red underwear shops are a famous local quirk (said to bring health and longevity). A great spot for authentic local interaction.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Asakusa via Tobu Nikko Line — budget ¥1,360 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine complex — an ornate and spectacular Edo-period shrine dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. The 'See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil' monkeys carving is here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine within the Nikko complex. Walk along the cedar-lined Omotesando approach. If time allows, take a local bus to Kegon Falls (¥550 for the elevator) — one of Japan's most famous waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Have a relaxed dinner near Tsukiji or pick up a convenience store bento for a rest night after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a local restaurant — a regional specialty (~¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Convenience store bento or simple ramen near hotel (~¥600–¥900)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited rides and discounts (¥4,780 from Asakusa — covers return train and local buses). Nikko's shrines charge a combined entry fee of ¥1,300. Start early to make the most of the day. April weather in Nikko may be cooler than Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets or another digital art experience in Toyosu (tickets ~¥3,200 — book in advance online). Alternatively, visit the free Toyosu Market outer viewing area to see the wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shibuya's Daikanyama and Nakameguro neighborhoods — stroll along the Meguro River (beautiful with late-season cherry blossoms or greenery in April). Browse the boutique shops and cafes in Daikanyama, including the iconic Tsutaya Books (a beautifully designed bookstore).
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Tokyo — return to Shibuya for the crossing experience at night, then explore the vibrant nightlife in the surrounding streets. Enjoy a farewell izakaya dinner with Japanese craft beer or sake.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local cafe (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Toyosu area sushi restaurant or food hall (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro or Shibuya izakaya farewell dinner (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets in Toyosu is a must-book-in-advance experience — check availability early in your trip. Nakameguro is one of Tokyo's most photogenic neighborhoods. The Meguro River canal lined with shops and cafes is a highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit your favorite spot near Tsukiji for a last breakfast at the Outer Market. Do any final souvenir shopping (Tsukiji has great food souvenirs like dried seaweed, bonito flakes, and wasabi). Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to the airport or squeeze in one last activity. Suggested: a final walk through Ginza or a quick visit to a 100-yen shop (Daiso) for last-minute budget souvenirs. Head to the airport via the Airport Limousine Bus or train.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days of food, tech culture, and local experiences.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market final breakfast — fresh sushi or tamagoyaki (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Airport terminal restaurant or bento from a convenience store (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport travel and check-in. Narita Airport is about 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Use remaining Suica/Pasmo balance at convenience stores or vending machines, or get a refund at the airport (¥220 handling fee). Export tax-free purchases must be declared at customs.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check into your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market, which stays lively into the afternoon. Browse fresh seafood stalls, street snacks, and local vendors to get your first taste of Tokyo's food culture. Pick up tamagoyaki (rolled egg), fresh fruit, and matcha treats as a light snack.
day_by_day.evening: Walk 10 minutes to the Hamarikyu Gardens for a peaceful early evening stroll along the waterfront — the garden offers beautiful views of Tokyo Bay and the city skyline, especially lovely in spring. Afterward, explore the nearby Shiodome district and enjoy dinner at a local izakaya on Shin-Ohashi Street.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a convenience store onigiri (7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel) upon arrival
meals.lunch: Street food snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market — try fresh oysters, tamagoyaki, and tuna skewers (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Tsukiji or Shiodome — order yakitori, edamame, and cold Sapporo beer (¥2,500–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: April 15 is mid-spring — expect mild temperatures around 14–20°C. Cherry blossoms may still be visible. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster. Suica or Pasmo card can be purchased at the airport for easy transit.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and visit Tsukiji Outer Market for a proper breakfast — this is one of Tokyo's most iconic food experiences. Try fresh sashimi breakfast sets, grilled scallops, and thick tamago sandwiches at the market stalls. Afterward, walk to Tsukiji Honganji Temple for a quiet morning visit to this stunning Buddhist temple with Indian-influenced architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, browse retro game shops, anime merchandise, and maid cafés. Visit the AKIBA Culture Zone for a deep dive into otaku and tech subculture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner, then explore the neon-lit streets after dark — the district transforms into a glowing spectacle at night. Visit a multi-floor arcade like Taito Station for a fun evening of Japanese gaming culture.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh sashimi don or grilled seafood set (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Akihabara shop — try Ichiran or a local tonkotsu ramen spot (¥900–¥1,300)
meals.dinner: Akihabara curry or katsu restaurant — try Coco Ichibanya or a local teishoku (set meal) restaurant (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Most electronics shops open around 10:00–11:00. If you're interested in tech gadgets, this is the best place to find unique Japanese electronics not available abroad. Duty-free shopping available with passport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive before 09:00 to beat the crowds. Walk through the Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes), and local crafts. Explore the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood's traditional shitamachi (old town) atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Sumida River via the scenic Azumabashi Bridge and visit the Tokyo Skytree — one of the world's tallest towers at 634 meters. Take the elevator to the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for Japanese design goods and food.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Yanaka Ginza — a charming retro shopping street that feels like old Tokyo. Browse independent shops, craft stores, and local eateries. Enjoy a traditional Japanese dinner in the Yanaka or Nezu neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa café breakfast or traditional Japanese set at a local kissaten (coffee shop) near Senso-ji (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solamachi food hall in Tokyo Skytree — try Tokyo-style sushi or wagyu beef bowl (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Traditional izakaya dinner in Yanaka — seasonal vegetable dishes, grilled fish, and sake (¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets: Tembo Deck costs approximately ¥2,100 for adults. Book online in advance to avoid queues. Asakusa and Yanaka are both very walkable and photogenic — bring your camera. The Sumida River area has beautiful cherry blossom trees in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shibuya — start with the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park overlooking the intersection. Visit the Hachiko Statue and explore the surrounding streets. Head to Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Hikarie for modern Tokyo architecture and design culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Harajuku and explore Takeshita Street for quirky fashion, crepes, and youth culture. Then shift to the elegant Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — lined with flagship stores from global and Japanese luxury brands. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex designed by architect Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — two of Tokyo's hippest neighborhoods. Walk along the Meguro River (beautiful with spring blossoms) and browse independent boutiques. Enjoy dinner at one of the trendy restaurants along the canal.

meals.breakfast: Shibuya bakery breakfast — Viron or a local artisan bakery near the hotel or in Shibuya (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe and snacks on Takeshita Street, plus a light meal at a Omotesando café (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro restaurant — try Italian-Japanese fusion or a farm-to-table Japanese restaurant along the canal (¥3,000–¥4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means crowds in Shibuya and Harajuku — arrive early. Takeshita Street is most vibrant on weekends. The Meguro River walk is especially beautiful if cherry blossoms are still in bloom. Comfortable walking shoes strongly recommended — expect 15,000+ steps.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — a serene Shinto shrine set within a forested park. Arrive early for a peaceful experience before crowds arrive. Watch for traditional Shinto ceremonies if scheduled. Walk through the forested path and enjoy the tranquility in contrast to the busy city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shinjuku — explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks and perfect for spring flower viewing. The garden has Japanese, French, and English garden sections. Afterward, explore the east side of Shinjuku around Kabukicho and the Golden Gai area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Golden Gai — a labyrinthine alley of tiny, atmospheric bars each seating only 5–8 people. This is one of Tokyo's most unique nightlife experiences. Choose a bar that welcomes tourists (most display welcome signs) and enjoy craft cocktails or Japanese whisky with locals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby Tsukiji market breakfast — fresh fish or Japanese set meal (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style — buy bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or depachika (department store basement food hall) at Isetan Shinjuku (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku ramen street or an izakaya near Golden Gai — try Fuunji for tsukemen (dipping ramen) or a local yakitori spot (¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry fee: approximately ¥500. Alcohol is not permitted inside the garden. Golden Gai bars typically charge a small cover fee (¥500–¥1,000) plus drinks. The area is safe but very small — be respectful of the intimate atmosphere. Some bars are reservation-only.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets in Toyosu (check current location for 2027) — Tokyo's world-famous immersive digital art museum. This is a must-see for tech and culture enthusiasts. Book tickets well in advance as they sell out weeks ahead. The experience takes 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) to explore cutting-edge Japanese robotics, AI, and space technology. See ASIMO robot demonstrations and interactive tech exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Odaiba for sunset views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and have dinner at one of the waterfront restaurants with bay views. The area is beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Tsukiji or hotel — Japanese morning set with miso soup, rice, and grilled fish (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at teamLab café or nearby Toyosu market food court — try fresh seafood from the new Toyosu Market (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Odaiba waterfront restaurant — try a mid-range Japanese restaurant with Tokyo Bay views (¥3,000–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be pre-booked online — typically ¥3,200–¥3,800 per person. Miraikan entry: approximately ¥630. Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi Station — the ride itself offers great views. Monday can be quieter at museums.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (approximately 2 hours). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex, one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrine complexes dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. Explore the Yomeimon Gate and surrounding cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Futarasan Shrine, and the scenic Shinkyo Bridge (Sacred Bridge) over the Daiya River. If time permits, take a short bus ride to Kegon Waterfall, one of Japan's most impressive waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (train back approximately 2 hours). Have a relaxed dinner near Tsukiji or in the Ginza neighborhood — a short walk from your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tsukiji before departure — onigiri and miso soup from a market stall (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty unique to Nikko, served at a traditional restaurant near the shrines (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Ginza restaurant — try a mid-range sushi bar or Japanese brasserie near Chuo City (¥3,000–¥4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Nikko day trip: Tobu Nikko All Area Pass recommended (approximately ¥4,780 from Asakusa — includes round-trip train and local buses). Tosho-gu entry: approximately ¥1,300. Wear comfortable shoes for walking on uneven stone paths. Spring in Nikko is beautiful with cherry blossoms and fresh greenery.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district, a short walk from your Tsukiji hotel. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a 12-floor design lover's paradise), browse the galleries at the Ginza Six complex, and admire the architecture of the Hermès Building and Apple Ginza.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest and oldest museum with an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ceramics, and cultural artifacts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the main Honkan building. Walk through Ueno Park afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively outdoor market street with food stalls, clothing, and goods. Great for people-watching and picking up affordable snacks. Have dinner in the Ueno or Akihabara area.

meals.breakfast: Ginza café breakfast — Café de l'Ambre (legendary Tokyo coffee institution) or a local bakery (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Ueno Park bento or Ueno museum café lunch — seasonal Japanese set meal (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ameyoko area yakitori or seafood dinner — casual standing bar or sit-down izakaya (¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum entry: approximately ¥1,000. Closed on Mondays (today is Wednesday — open). Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji in about 15 minutes. Itoya stationery store is free to browse and is a wonderful cultural experience for design enthusiasts. Ameyoko is most lively in the late afternoon and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka Cemetery and the Yanaka neighborhood — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic districts that survived WWII bombing. Stroll through the cemetery's cherry tree-lined paths (beautiful in spring), visit local temples, and explore the artistic community of craftspeople and independent shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Koenji — a bohemian neighborhood known for vintage clothing stores, record shops, indie cafés, and alternative culture. This is Tokyo's answer to Brooklyn — creative, affordable, and authentically local. Browse the dozens of vintage clothing shops along the covered shotengai (shopping arcade).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo and visit the Roppongi Arts Triangle — explore Mori Art Museum (contemporary art with panoramic city views from the 53rd floor) or the National Art Center Tokyo. Enjoy dinner in the Roppongi or Azabu area.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) breakfast in Yanaka — toast, eggs, and coffee set (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Koenji café lunch — try a local curry shop or ramen restaurant popular with locals (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Roppongi mid-range restaurant — try Japanese-French fusion or a quality teppanyaki restaurant (¥3,500–¥5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum entry: approximately ¥2,000 (includes Tokyo City View observation deck). Yanaka and Koenji are both best explored on foot and by bicycle. Koenji vintage shops typically open around 12:00–13:00. This day gives a wonderful contrast between old and alternative Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab or explore the Toyosu Fish Market (new Tsukiji) — if you haven't visited the new wholesale market, morning tours are available from around 05:30. Alternatively, visit the Panasonic Center Tokyo or Sony Park for a tech culture experience. Head to Marunouchi and the Imperial Palace East Gardens for a morning walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Marunouchi and Nihonbashi districts — Tokyo's historic financial and commercial heart. Visit Coredo Muromachi for beautifully curated Japanese craft goods, traditional sweets, and design items. Walk across the historic Nihonbashi Bridge (the zero-point of all Japanese highways).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Japanese performing arts experience — book tickets for Kabuki at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza (single-act tickets available for approximately ¥1,000–¥2,500 without advance booking). This is one of Tokyo's most culturally immersive evening experiences.

meals.breakfast: Nihonbashi depachika (department store basement) — pick up a beautiful Japanese breakfast from Mitsukoshi or Takashimaya food halls (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Coredo Muromachi food hall — try traditional soba noodles at a quality Nihonbashi soba restaurant (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Pre-theater dinner in Ginza — kaiseki bento or quality Japanese set meal near Kabukiza (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kabukiza Theatre single-act (hitomaku-mi) tickets are available on the day at the box office — arrive 30–60 minutes before the act. English audio guides available for ¥700. This is a Friday — Ginza will be lively in the evening. Nihonbashi area is excellent for purchasing high-quality Japanese crafts and food souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (approximately 1 hour). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Temple) — a 13-meter bronze Buddha statue dating from 1252. Explore Hase-dera Temple with its stunning views of Sagami Bay and beautiful gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through the forested hills connecting several temples and shrines. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important Shinto shrine with a grand approach lined with cherry trees. Browse the charming Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Tsukiji area. Explore the local neighborhood around your hotel and try a small neighborhood restaurant you haven't visited yet.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tsukiji market before departure — fresh fish, miso soup, and rice (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Kamakura shirasu (whitebait) cuisine — a local specialty served as rice bowls or on pizza at restaurants near Hase Station (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood restaurant near Tsukiji hotel — try a local sushi counter or Japanese home-cooking restaurant (¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: JR Pass or Suica card covers the Kamakura train fare (approximately ¥940 each way). Great Buddha entry: ¥300. Hase-dera entry: ¥400. Kamakura is very popular on weekends — arrive early. The hiking trail takes approximately 1.5–2 hours and requires sturdy shoes. Spring wildflowers and fresh greenery make the hike especially scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (check if renovations are complete by 2027) or the Sumida Hokusai Museum — a stunning Kengo Kuma-designed building dedicated to the ukiyo-e master Katsushika Hokusai. Learn about Edo-period Tokyo through art and cultural artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Watch a sumo practice session — Ryogoku is Tokyo's sumo district. Visit the Kokugikan Sumo Arena and the nearby Sumo Museum. If a tournament is scheduled (check 2027 calendar), tickets can be purchased for an afternoon session. Alternatively, visit a sumo stable for a morning practice viewing (requires advance arrangement).
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening out — head to Tokyo Tower for night views of the city (a more intimate and classic experience compared to Skytree). Walk through the Shiba Park area and enjoy dinner in the upscale Azabu-Juban neighborhood, known for its international food scene and local charm.

meals.breakfast: Ryogoku chankonabe breakfast or brunch — the hearty stew traditionally eaten by sumo wrestlers, available at local restaurants near the Kokugikan (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.lunch: Ryogoku local restaurant — try a traditional teishoku (set meal) with grilled fish and pickles (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Azabu-Juban restaurant — choose from excellent Japanese, French, or international cuisine in this cosmopolitan neighborhood (¥3,500–¥5,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Tower observation deck entry: approximately ¥1,200 (Main Deck at 150m). The Sumida Hokusai Museum entry: approximately ¥400. Sumo tournaments in Tokyo are held in January, May, and September — April 2027 may not have a tournament, but the museum and stable visits are available year-round. Azabu-Juban is one of Tokyo's most pleasant neighborhoods for a final evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — return to Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell breakfast and last-minute food shopping. Pick up Japanese food souvenirs: premium dashi packs, wasabi, nori, Japanese sweets (wagashi), and any other pantry items. Visit the nearby Namiyoke Inari Shrine for a final blessing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if afternoon flight: head to the airport after checkout (allow 2.5–3 hours before flight). If evening flight: visit the Ginza neighborhood one last time for any final shopping at Itoya, Matsuya, or Mitsukoshi department store. Pick up omiyage (souvenir gifts) from the basement food halls.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. If time allows before heading to the airport, enjoy a final bowl of ramen or sushi near the hotel as a farewell meal. Take the Narita Express or Airport Limousine Bus to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh uni (sea urchin) or toro (fatty tuna) don as a splurge farewell meal (¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.lunch: Ginza depachika bento or airport terminal restaurant — quality Japanese set meal (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Airport terminal dinner at Narita or Haneda — many excellent ramen and sushi options available airside (¥1,500–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00–12:00) and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Narita Express takes approximately 60–90 minutes to Narita Airport. Haneda Airport is closer (30–40 minutes via monorail or Keikyu Line). Japanese customs allows up to ¥200,000 worth of goods duty-free. Pack food items carefully — some fresh items may not be allowed through customs on return.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in — Flight lands at 13:00; clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or a private airport transfer to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Settle in, freshen up, and orient yourself with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Afternoon Stroll — Even arriving mid-afternoon, the Outer Market remains lively. Take a leisurely self-guided walk through the covered stalls sampling tamagoyaki (rolled egg omelette), fresh-grilled seafood skewers, and artisan pickles. Pick up a premium matcha soft-serve from one of the renowned vendors as a welcome-to-Tokyo treat.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito-style Omakase — Book a coveted counter seat at a high-end Tsukiji-area sushi restaurant (e.g., Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Sho in nearby Yotsuya) for a full omakase experience featuring the day's finest catch. End the night with a quiet walk along the Sumida River waterfront, admiring the illuminated Rainbow Bridge in the distance.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi counter in Tsukiji/Ginza area — expect 20–35 courses of nigiri with seasonal accompaniments; budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the omakase dinner well in advance (months ahead if possible). Consider hiring a private car from Narita for a stress-free first arrival. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Guided Food Tour — Join the premium Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour at opening time. A knowledgeable local guide leads you through the labyrinthine alleys, introducing you to legendary vendors: uni (sea urchin) on rice crackers, tuna sashimi tastings, hand-rolled tamago, and aged dashi broths. Learn the history of Japan's most iconic food district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ginza Luxury & Culture Walk — A 10-minute walk from Tsukiji, Ginza is Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and arts district. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (9 floors of Japanese craftsmanship), browse the Ginza Six mall's rooftop garden, and explore the Mori Arts exhibition or the Hermès Maison Ginza gallery. Stop into Mikimoto for a look at cultured pearl heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Kaiseki Dinner in Ginza — Dine at a celebrated kaiseki restaurant such as Koju (1 Michelin star) or Ginza Kojyu for a multi-course seasonal Japanese haute cuisine experience. Each course reflects the spring season — expect cherry blossom-themed presentations, bamboo shoots, and sakura-cured fish.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Tsukiji's famous fresh tuna rice bowl (maguro don) at Tsukiji Yamamotoya
meals.lunch: Tsukiji food tour tastings serve as a substantial late-morning meal; supplement with a bowl of high-grade ramen at Ginza Kagari
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Koju or Ginza Kojyu — ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The food tour typically starts at 08:00–09:00; confirm timing with the operator. Ginza shops open around 11:00. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone market walking.

day_by_day.morning: teamLab Borderless (Odaiba or Azabudai Hills) — Take the Yurikamome monorail or a taxi to the newly relocated teamLab Borderless digital art museum at Azabudai Hills. Spend 2–3 hours immersed in boundaryless digital art installations — a perfect intersection of Japanese tech culture and artistic tradition. The spring edition features sakura-themed projections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Odaiba Tech & Pop Culture — Head to Odaiba's DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue, then explore the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robot demonstrations, AI exhibits, and a stunning Geo-Cosmos globe. End at the Toyota Mega Web showroom for a glimpse of next-generation mobility concepts.
day_by_day.evening: Waterfront Dinner with Rainbow Bridge Views — Dine at a premium restaurant in Odaiba's Aqua City complex or the InterContinental Tokyo Bay. Try Tempura Kondo (if returning to Ginza) or enjoy teppanyaki at Ukai-tei Ginza for theatrical tableside cooking with A5 Wagyu beef.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and pastries at Turret Coffee in Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Ramen or donburi at a quality counter in Odaiba's food hall, or a bento from a Miraikan café
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki A5 Wagyu at Ukai-tei Ginza — ¥25,000–¥45,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets online in advance — timed entry slots sell out weeks ahead. The Yurikamome monorail offers spectacular bay views en route to Odaiba.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Immersion — Take a short taxi or subway ride to Asakusa. Arrive early at Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, before the crowds. Stroll the Nakamise shopping street for premium crafts: hand-painted fans, lacquerware, and traditional sweets (ningyo-yaki). Hire a rickshaw (jinrikisha) for a 30-minute guided neighborhood tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sumida & Hamarikyu Gardens — Walk south along the Sumida River to the stunning Hamarikyu Gardens, a 17th-century feudal lord's garden with a tidal pond, teahouses, and seasonal flowers. Enjoy a traditional matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) ceremony at the garden's authentic teahouse overlooking the pond. Cross the garden to the Shiodome skyscraper district.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Cocktails & Yakiniku Dinner — Head to the Park Hotel Tokyo's Artist Room bar or the Conrad Tokyo for sunset cocktails with panoramic city views. Dinner at Yakiniku Jumbo Hanare or Aragawa steakhouse — considered one of Japan's finest, serving legendary Kobe beef in an intimate, club-like setting.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan for a traditional Japanese breakfast set, or ningyo-yaki and matcha from Nakamise stalls
meals.lunch: Matcha and wagashi tea ceremony at Hamarikyu teahouse (light but ceremonial)
meals.dinner: Aragawa steakhouse or premium yakiniku — ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24/7; arriving before 08:00 ensures a tranquil atmosphere. Hamarikyu Gardens charges a small entry fee. Book Aragawa months in advance — it seats very few guests.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Crossing & Scramble Sky Deck — Travel to Shibuya, Tokyo's most energetic district. Start with a bird's-eye view of the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing from Shibuya Sky observation deck (rooftop, 230m high). Then descend into the crossing itself for the full sensory experience. Visit the Shibuya Stream and Scramble Square for contemporary Japanese design and retail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku & Omotesando Luxury Avenue — Walk north to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for a peek at Japan's quirky youth fashion subculture, then pivot to the elegant Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées. Explore the architecturally iconic Prada, Louis Vuitton, and Comme des Garçons flagships. Visit the Nezu Museum for a serene collection of Japanese and Asian antiquities in a bamboo garden setting.
day_by_day.evening: Omakase Tempura or French-Japanese Fusion — Dine at Tempura Kondo in Ginza (legendary light batter technique) or L'Effervescence in Nishi-Azabu for innovative French-Japanese cuisine using foraged Japanese ingredients. Both hold Michelin stars and offer intimate counter or table experiences.

meals.breakfast: Café Kitsuné in Omotesando or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gyukatsu Motomura for premium breaded beef cutlet, or a delicate bento at a Omotesando café
meals.dinner: Tempura Kondo (Ginza) or L'Effervescence (Nishi-Azabu) — ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky tickets should be booked online. Sunday in Harajuku is peak street fashion day. The Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in cherry blossom or spring greenery season.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive — Dedicate the morning to Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera) for the latest Japanese gadgets unavailable elsewhere. Visit Akihabara's retro game shops for rare Nintendo and Sega collectibles, and explore the Radio Kaikan building for hobby and tech culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Robot Restaurant or Maid Café Culture & Akihabara Anime — Experience the intersection of Japanese tech culture and pop entertainment: visit the Gundam Café, explore the Kotobukiya figurine store, and browse the sprawling Mandarake complex for anime and manga history. For a uniquely Japanese tech-entertainment experience, book the Henn na Hotel robot-staffed café experience or a premium maid café like @home café.
day_by_day.evening: Kanda Yabu Soba & Sake Tasting — Travel to nearby Kanda for dinner at the historic Kanda Yabu Soba (est. 1880), one of Tokyo's most revered soba restaurants, for hand-cut buckwheat noodles in refined dashi broth. Follow with a curated sake tasting at Hasegawa Saketen in Tokyo Skytree Town or a sake bar in nearby Nihonbashi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a morning set at a Doutor or artisan coffee shop near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Akihabara's UDX building food floor — try Japanese curry at CoCo Ichibanya premium or a high-grade tonkatsu set
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba followed by sake bar — ¥8,000–¥15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best on weekday mornings to avoid weekend crowds. Many electronics stores offer tax-free shopping for tourists — bring your passport. Kanda Yabu Soba may have queues; arrive at opening time.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — Begin the day at one of Tokyo's most magnificent gardens, especially glorious in mid-April with late cherry blossoms and spring blooms. Stroll the French Formal, English Landscape, and Japanese Traditional garden sections. Bring a premium bento from a Shinjuku depachika (department store basement food hall) for a picnic under the blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinjuku Kabukicho & Golden Gai Exploration — Explore the vibrant Kabukicho entertainment district in daylight, visiting the iconic Godzilla head atop the Toho Cinema building. Wander the atmospheric Golden Gai — a grid of over 200 tiny, intimate bars, each with its own character. By day, many are open for coffee and conversation with locals. Visit the Samurai Museum nearby for an interactive cultural experience with armor fittings.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Dinner in Shinjuku — Dine at Kozue, the acclaimed Japanese restaurant on the 40th floor of the Park Hyatt Tokyo (setting of Lost in Translation), with panoramic views over the city. Enjoy seasonal Japanese cuisine paired with premium sake. Afterwards, visit the New York Bar at the Park Hyatt for jazz and cocktails with the Tokyo skyline as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Isetan Shinjuku B1 food hall morning pastries
meals.lunch: Premium bento picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen from Isetan's basement food hall (depachika)
meals.dinner: Kozue at Park Hyatt Tokyo — ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person; New York Bar for nightcaps

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen has a small entry fee and no alcohol permitted inside. Book Kozue and New York Bar well in advance — they are iconic and popular with international visitors. Golden Gai bars begin opening around 18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka Historic District & Old Tokyo Shitamachi — Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved pre-war neighborhoods. Wander the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (old shopping street), visit the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery (a peaceful sakura spot), and browse artisan craft studios and independent pottery shops. This area offers an authentic window into Edo-period Tokyo life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Museums & Cultural Afternoon — Walk to Ueno Park, home to Japan's finest concentration of museums. Choose between the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest, with priceless samurai swords, ceramics, and Buddhist art), the National Museum of Western Art (Le Corbusier building, UNESCO-listed), or the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum for contemporary exhibitions. End with a stroll through Ueno Park's pond and pagoda.
day_by_day.evening: Nihonbashi Fine Dining — Take a short taxi to Nihonbashi, Tokyo's historic mercantile heart. Dine at Nihonbashi Yukari (three Michelin stars) for exquisite traditional Japanese cuisine in an elegant setting, or try Harutaka for a celebrated sushi omakase. Explore the beautifully restored Nihonbashi bridge and Coredo Muromachi complex afterwards.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Coffee or a traditional Japanese breakfast at a neighborhood kissaten (retro café)
meals.lunch: Handmade udon or soba at a Yanaka or Ueno area restaurant; try Ueno Yabu Soba
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi Yukari (3 Michelin stars) — ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Pre-book dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari — reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba & Sony ExploraScience / Digital Frontier — Return to the tech-forward waterfront district for a deeper dive. Visit Sony's interactive ExploraScience center or the newly opened Sony Park in Ginza for immersive product and innovation experiences. Alternatively, explore the Panasonic Center Tokyo for cutting-edge smart home and sustainability technology demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Toyosu Market VIP Tour — Book a premium behind-the-scenes tour of Toyosu Market, the world's largest wholesale seafood market (successor to Tsukiji's inner market). Watch the legendary tuna auction from the observation deck (early morning slots are most dramatic, but afternoon facility tours are available), learn about Japan's seafood supply chain, and visit the premium sushi restaurants within the market complex.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito or Sushi Sawada — This is the evening for Tokyo's ultimate sushi experience. Sushi Sawada (3 Michelin stars, Ginza) or Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) offer the pinnacle of Edomae sushi tradition. Each piece is crafted to perfection with aged fish, hand-pressed rice, and house-made nikiri soy. A once-in-a-lifetime meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or premium tamago gohan (egg over rice) at a specialist Tsukiji café
meals.lunch: Sushi or seafood donburi at Toyosu Market's Sushidai or Itadori restaurant
meals.dinner: Sushi Sawada or Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) — ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person; book months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction observation requires advance lottery registration through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. The afternoon facility tour is easier to access. Three-Michelin-star sushi reservations require months of advance planning, often through a hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Yoyogi Park — Begin with a serene morning at Meiji Jingu, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, set within a forested 70-hectare urban sanctuary. Participate in a morning ritual or simply walk the grand torii-lined approach. Stroll through adjacent Yoyogi Park, alive with spring greenery, street musicians, and weekend practitioners of traditional arts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Daikanyama & Nakameguro Premium Lifestyle — Explore Daikanyama, Tokyo's most refined residential-retail neighborhood. Visit the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural complex with a premium café. Walk the Meguro River canal lined with cherry blossom trees (late bloomers in mid-April) through Nakameguro's boutique-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Ebisu & Daikanyama Dinner — Dine at Chez Panisse-inspired Tirpse in Minami-Aoyama or the celebrated Florilège (2 Michelin stars) in Aoyama for boundary-pushing Japanese-French cuisine. Alternatively, enjoy an intimate dinner at Daikanyama's Ivy Place for a sophisticated international menu in a garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee at Log Road Daikanyama's premium café
meals.lunch: Daikanyama T-Site Anjin café for a beautifully presented seasonal Japanese lunch set
meals.dinner: Florilège (2 Michelin stars, Aoyama) — ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is most peaceful before 09:00. Daikanyama T-Site is a must-visit for design and culture lovers — the architecture alone is worth the trip. Nakameguro is particularly beautiful during late cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Roppongi Art Triangle — Spend the morning exploring Roppongi's world-class art institutions. Start at the Mori Art Museum (52nd floor of Mori Tower) for contemporary Japanese and international art with sweeping city views. Then visit the National Art Center Tokyo (largest exhibition space in Japan) and the Suntory Museum of Art for traditional Japanese decorative arts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Azabudai Hills & Minami-Azabu Exploration — Walk to the newly completed Azabudai Hills megadevelopment — a landmark fusion of architecture, art, nature, and technology. Explore the public art installations, visit the Heatherwick Studio-designed gardens, browse the premium retail and gallery spaces, and take in the innovative urban design that represents Tokyo's future vision.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi Hills Club Dinner — Dine at one of Roppongi Hills' premium restaurants: Inakaya (famous robatayaki grill where chefs pass food on long wooden paddles) for a theatrical and delicious experience, or the sophisticated Japanese-French fusion at L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon Tokyo for a Michelin-starred counter experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium breakfast set at a Roppongi Hills café
meals.lunch: Azabudai Hills food market — curated artisan Japanese food stalls and premium bento
meals.dinner: Inakaya Roppongi (robatayaki) or L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon — ¥20,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on most days) — consider visiting in the evening for city night views. Azabudai Hills is a short walk from Roppongi. Book L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon counter seats in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Nikko or Hakone Day Trip Option — For a premium day trip, take the Shinkansen or a private car to Nikko (2 hours), home to the opulent Tosho-gu shrine complex, UNESCO-listed mausoleums of Tokugawa Ieyasu, and cedar-lined sacred avenues. Alternatively, head to Hakone (1.5 hours) for views of Mt. Fuji, open-air sculpture museums, and ryokan culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nikko Sacred Grounds or Hakone Open-Air Museum — In Nikko: explore the elaborately carved Yomeimon Gate, the serene Futarasan Shrine, and the peaceful Rinno-ji temple gardens. In Hakone: visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum (stunning sculpture park), ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani, and enjoy views of Fuji-san if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo & Farewell Kaiseki — Return to Tokyo by early evening. For the penultimate night, indulge in a special farewell-style dinner at Kagurazaka Ishikawa (3 Michelin stars) — an intimate, exquisitely crafted kaiseki experience in a traditional machiya townhouse setting, regarded as one of Tokyo's finest dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: In Nikko: yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at Gyoshintei restaurant; in Hakone: soba at a mountain restaurant
meals.dinner: Kagurazaka Ishikawa (3 Michelin stars) — ¥35,000–¥50,000 per person; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Depart Tokyo by 08:00–09:00 for a comfortable day trip. A private car hire for the Nikko or Hakone day trip is recommended for maximum flexibility and comfort. Kagurazaka Ishikawa reservations require months of advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Tsukiji & Ginza — Spend a final leisurely morning in your home neighborhood. Return to the Tsukiji Outer Market for last-minute food souvenirs: premium dashi packets, yuzu kosho, matcha powder, and artisan soy sauce. Visit the Tsukiji Honganji Temple nearby for a quiet moment of reflection. Pack and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ginza Souvenir Shopping & Farewell Lunch — Head to Ginza for premium souvenir shopping: Itoya for Japanese stationery, Mikimoto for pearl jewelry, Takashimaya or Mitsukoshi for beautifully wrapped wagashi sweets and gift sets. Enjoy a final Tokyo lunch at a celebrated tempura or soba restaurant before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport via private car or Narita Express. Depart Tokyo with extraordinary memories of food, technology, culture, and the singular magic of one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: One final fresh tuna rice bowl or tamagoyaki sandwich from a beloved Tsukiji vendor
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Ten-ichi (Ginza) for legendary tempura — a Tokyo institution since 1930 — ¥8,000–¥15,000 per person
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at Haneda's premium ANA Suite Lounge or TIAT Sky Suite

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Most premium airlines offer private airport transfer services — arrange through your hotel concierge. Declare any food items at customs. Japan's duty-free allowances apply to purchases made with your passport.
